control.notes: Study is a cross-population comparison, not a case-control design.

country.evidence_quote: we generated shotgun metagenomic data of semi-isolated Yanomami from Brazil
country.notes: Tunapuco country not explicitly stated; only 'Andean highlands' mentioned.

body_site.evidence_quote: Participants were requested to provide a morning fecal sample
body_site.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
body_site.notes: Applies to all groups as the study is a gut microbiome (fecal) comparison.

days_from_first_collection.notes: Single cross-sectional stool sample per subject; no longitudinal timepoints reported.

lifestyle.evidence_quote: The Yanomami group is mainly hunter–gatherers, but in some communities, the women cultivate plantains and cassava, while men go hunting.
lifestyle.section: Results — Lifestyle of the Human Group Studied
lifestyle.notes: Matses/Yanomami Venezuela described as 'hunter–gatherer communities'; Tunapuco described as 'rural agricultural community'; US not assigned a lifestyle category here (urban-industrialized).

westernized.evidence_quote: compared taxonomically and functionally with the Yanomami from Venezuela, with other traditional groups from the Amazon and an urban-industrialized group
westernized.notes: Traditional groups (Yanomami/Brazil, Yanomami/Venezuela, Matses, Tunapuco) contrasted with the 'urban-industrialized' US group.

ncbi_accession.evidence_quote: The datasets generated for this study can be found in the NCBI under the BioProject PRJNA527208.
ncbi_accession.notes: Accession applies only to newly generated Yanomami/Brazil metagenomes; other datasets are from previously published studies (accessions not given in this paper).

age.evidence_quote: At the time of the collection, age and gender information of the individuals were also acquired. These details are summarized in Supplementary Table 1.
age.section: Methods — Study Participants and Sample Collection
age.notes: Age data collected but reported only in Supplementary Table 1, not included in provided text.

sex.evidence_quote: Association between gut microbiome composition and gender was analyzed with principal coordinate analysis (PcoA)
sex.section: Results — Intra- and Inter-Individual Diversity of the Gut Microbiomes
sex.notes: Gender was analyzed but specific counts/sex per subject not reported in main text.

dietary_restriction.notes: Diet described qualitatively (fiber-rich, fruits, sylvatic animals) but no formal dietary restriction category reported.

disease.evidence_quote: Common chronic diseases in modern societies, as atherosclerosis and obesity are virtually unknown among Yanomami
disease.notes: Statement is a general epidemiological observation about the Yanomami population, not a direct disease-screening statement for the specific study participants; inferred as 'Healthy' with low confidence.

disease_details.notes: Paper describes healthy traditional hunter-gatherer populations but does not explicitly assign a disease/health status label to participants.

disease_response_orr.notes: No treatment/clinical response data reported; this is a microbiome ecology study.

disease_response_pfs.notes: Not applicable; no oncology treatment context.

feces_phenotype.notes: Stool samples were collected but no specific stool phenotype (e.g., Bristol scale) was reported.

treatment.notes: No pharmacological or clinical treatment administered or reported.

biomarker_name.notes: Paper discusses taxonomic/functional 'biomarkers' of gut microbiome groups, not clinical biomarkers with quantifiable values matching this schema's intent.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Not applicable to this study (gut microbiome research, no tumor-related measurements).

study_name.notes: No canonical study identifier (e.g., AuthorX_Year) explicitly stated in the paper text provided.

pmid.notes: PubMed ID not explicitly stated within the body text provided; paper_id supplied externally cannot be used as source evidence.

target_condition.notes: Study investigates gut microbiome composition/diversity related to lifestyle (hunter-gatherer vs urban-industrialized), not a specific disease phenotype; no explicit 'target condition' or disease outcome is defined as the study focus.
